title: Finish The Artwork And Show Its Making
objective: Complete the pupil’s new print-and-collage artwork and assemble a trace of its actual making that includes both process evidence and the final work.

blocks.text: Explore · Part C · Create. Finish the artwork and show its making.
Today you will finish your new collage and show how you made it. You will keep the final work with real records of the steps that led to it.
We are making a new print and collage. A print is a mark pressed from one surface to another. A collage joins pieces to make one image.
Part C needs an artwork, its making process and the final work. A plan alone does not show the making. A final image alone does not show the steps you took.
You can point, speak, type or write to show your choices. You may make a pattern or a made-up place. Your art does not have to tell a story about your life.

This deck supports Explore Part C, Create. Part C requires an artwork, a record of the PROCESS, and the final work. The new print-and-collage activity is distinct from the drawing and paper sculpture in Part A and the live or active exploration in Part B. Do not relabel a finished A or B work as C. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. Mark each part P / A / N. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. The whole Explore digital portfolio has a 10-file cap. Organise it by part; four cumulative files, Explore-A, Explore-B, Explore-C and Explore-D, are a suggested arrangement, not one new file per lesson. Every evidence locator must name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Explore; each retains the pupil’s own artwork, process record and final work across C1–C4. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm these conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Adults may scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back. They must not write plans, reviews or evidence for the pupil. Staff may record factual observations of access support separately. No visit, booking, meeting or date is asserted. Keep the theme on art choices; no private life account is required.

Explore Part C C4 completes and records the distinct print-and-collage artwork developed in C1–C3. Retrieve actual current work, earlier samples and saved states. Prepare glue sticks, dry spare paper, mats and access tools for finishing. Provide a safe drying place and a way to capture the whole final artwork as a clear image or scan; retain the actual work. Record who made each image and follow local consent rules without requiring faces or public posting. Model finishing and capture on adult work before independent pupil work. Check process and final evidence separately. If work is unfinished or a process record is absent, name the gap and arrange actual completion or a genuinely new recorded making step; do not recreate a false past account. The 40-minute session does not certify completion of the whole programme.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Set out your current artwork and the records you kept while making it. Find the start idea, a test, and a later state. You may have a sample, sketch, photo or short account.
Look back at the effect you wanted. Does your work now show it? Point to a part that is ready and a part that still needs care.
Choose a useful last step. You may need to fix a loose edge, finish a planned section, or clear spare scraps from the backing. You do not have to fill every space.

stages.data-ta1: Retrieve only actual records. Prompts are scaffolds rather than required numbers of samples. Help pupils find existing evidence without adding a missing account in the pupil’s voice.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Imagine two records of an artwork. The first has only a finished image. The second has only a sketch of what the maker hoped to do. What can each record show? What is missing?
The finished image shows what was made, but not how it grew. The sketch shows a start idea, but not that the maker went on to make the work.
Our record will join real making steps to the final piece. It helps someone follow your choices from the first test to the artwork you have now.
You can keep a short, clear trail. You do not need a long story. Each part should show or name something you actually did with your own work.

stages.data-ta1: Keep both example cases hypothetical. Do not present the examples as pupil evidence. Check that pupils can identify why both process and final work are required.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch me finish my model. I look at the whole work before I touch it. The path is clear, but one paper edge lifts from the backing.
I keep a view of this state. Then I raise only the loose corner, add a little glue underneath, and press it flat with a clean scrap over the top. I check it again when it is ready.
I stop adding pieces because the open space is part of my idea. More paper would cover the gaps I chose. Finishing can mean knowing when to stop.
To keep the final view, I lay the dry work flat in even light. I include all four edges and keep my hand out of the frame. I check the image is sharp enough to see the prints and joins.

blocks.title: Finish and keep the whole work
blocks.caption: Keep the final work as well as the steps that led to it.
blocks.alt: CHECK: look at the full piece. FINISH: complete a real last step. CAPTURE: show every edge. LINK: join process and final. Keep the final work as well as the steps that led to it.

blocks.text: I keep the actual artwork too. If a scan gives a clearer view of this flat piece, I can use that. I name who captured the image so the record is clear.

stages.data-ta1: Model a real finishing action and clear capture of the whole dry artwork. Use a scan or approved image route. No pupil must appear in an image. Do not flatten wet paint on a scanner.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

blocks.text: Sort these record cards into PROCESS, FINAL WORK, or NEXT ACTION. Say or point to the group for each number before we check the key.

items: 1. A test strip shows the marks made with two paint coats.
2. A clear scan shows the whole finished collage.
3. A saved image shows the loose layout before its pieces were fixed.
4. I need to finish the last section before I record it as done.
5. My note says why I chose a small pale strip during making.

blocks.text: The key is PROCESS: 1, 3 and 5; FINAL WORK: 2; NEXT ACTION: 4. A next action is useful, but it is not proof that the action has happened.
Which two groups must be present for the complete Part C record? We need process and final work. Keep any next action honest until it is done.

stages.data-ta1: Use the visible cards and key without an extra sheet. Gather all responses before revealing the key. Distinguish pending work from actual evidence without judging a pupil’s speed.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: I put my first test and loose layout before the later state. I place the final image after them. I check that these records all belong to the same new artwork.

blocks.title: Two parts of one making record
blocks.caption: Both belong together in the Part C record.
blocks.alt: PROCESS: tests, stages and choices, show how the work grew. FINAL WORK: whole finished artwork, show what was made. Both belong together in the Part C record.

blocks.text: Under the layout I write: I moved the strip to leave a wider gap. Under the final image I write: This is my finished path collage. My words fit what the records show.
I open the saved file and note the page for each record. The words in my arts log do not tell a reader where to look. I need the real file name and a page, slide or timecode.
I do not remove an early test just because it looks less neat. It shows a part of the process that the final work cannot show by itself.

stages.data-ta1: Model opening a real file and finding an exact location. Do not give a fictional locator as if already saved. Keep original process records when adding the final image.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: With a partner or adult, check your work from edge to edge. Look for loose pieces and any last step that belongs to your idea. Ask before touching someone else’s artwork.
Try a view of the whole work. Can you see the corners and the print marks? Move the camera or scan setting if an edge is cut off. Credit the person who helps capture it.
Now find a process record that matches part of the work. Point to the link between them. If you cannot find one, tell an adult what is missing so the gap can be checked.

stages.data-ta1: This is a practice check; label work final only after actual completion. Help locate records or arrange further genuine making if process evidence is absent. Never fabricate an earlier state.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Carry out your last chosen making step. Preserve a state before a change. When the work is ready, keep a clear view of the whole final piece and store the artwork safely.
Add the final record beside your real tests, stages and choice notes. Put them in an order that helps a reader follow the making. Check that your own words match your work.

items: Core: use access tools and a helper to steady or capture the work. Make your own final choice. Point or speak to link your kept process records to the whole final artwork.
Extend: complete your last step, then order and label your real process records and final artwork. Explain a choice in your own words.
Challenge: complete the same process and final record. Trace how an early trial shaped a later choice, using your actual work to show the link.

blocks.text: If the work needs more time, say which step is left. Keep the part you have made and arrange time to finish. Do not label an unfinished image as the final piece.

stages.data-ta1: All routes must retain both process and final work. Scribe exact words only and check back. Staff may organise technical capture but may not supply the pupil’s choices or review. Allow actual completion time where needed.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Open your Explore-C file and point to the final artwork. Then find a record of how you made it. Check both can be seen or heard clearly.
Write the actual file name and page or slide for each. If you used a recording, add the file name and timecode. Keep the image credit with each captured view.
Is your work finished, or is a next step still needed? Record that truthfully. In Part D you will look across A, B and C to choose an enjoyment or achievement to share.

stages.data-ta1: Check actual evidence, locators and any completion gap. Append to the existing Part C file within the whole-portfolio cap. Do not claim Part D sharing has happened during this record check.

print.intro: Finish your own new artwork and keep a clear view of the whole piece. Join it to records of the real steps you took.
focusRows: My last making step and whether the artwork is complete
Real process records that show my tests, stages or choices
The whole final artwork, with my own label and image credit
Actual Explore-C file name plus page, slide or timecode for process and final work
tiers: Core: use access help to finish and capture your own work. Point or speak to link kept process records with the final artwork.
Extend: finish, order and label your own process records and final artwork. Explain a real choice.
Challenge: retain the same process and final artwork; trace how an early trial shaped a later choice.
checks: The new artwork is my own distinct Part C creation.
Real records show the process of making it.
The final work is complete and its whole image is clear, or I have named a real completion gap.
My words and image credits match what actually happened.
Both process and final work have actual file names and page, slide or timecode locators.
